Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

beginning noun

also start, origin, commencement, outset, at the beginning, in the beginning, from the beginning

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.54: orīgō prīncipiī nūlla est: nam ex prīncipiō oriuntur omnia (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 78: nec prīncipium, nec fīnem habēre (Lewis & Short)

prīncipium, prīncipiī n.

noun, second declension

a beginning, an origin

As adverbs prīncipiō, ā prīncipiō and in prīncipiō mean at first, in the beginning (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • initium, initiī n. — a beginning, a start

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.1: initium capere (Lewis & Short); Cic. Rosc. Am. 14: ab initiō rēs quem ad modum facta sint, expōnēmus (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • orīgō prīncipiī nūlla est: nam ex prīncipiō oriuntur omnia

    a beginning has no origin, for all things arise from a beginningCic. Tusc. 1.54 (Lewis & Short)

  • ā Jove prīncipium

    the beginning is from JoveVerg. E. 3.60 (Lewis & Short)

See also begin, source, original, all along, end.
